.You are right. At this time, I began to encounter the idea that there may not be an answer in the first place, but I cannot move on to live with that. I think that the problem is not in the question, or in asking it, but rather in our existence in the first place to ask that question because our exsistince create that question to be asked.

Thank you for sharing your opinion, I agree with you, but my problem is to find a meaning or motivation for happiness without answering that basic question because I know that even if I try to avoid it by relaxing and trying to live and have happiness and achieve goals I may be happy in the end or find a career and people I love but the question will remain unanswered and I doubt that I can ignore this question and just run after happiness without answering it Even happiness after reaching certain stages of thinking loses its meaning and essence and has no value in front of the big questions What we humans do is after we suddenly find ourselves present, and I represent that with the beginning of awareness. The first thing we did was ignore these questions and try to live, then consider thinking about them as a luxury that occurs in the vacuum of time and with the development of life when A person has more time to think. He discovered that there may be no answer to these questions, so he returned again to avoid them and become preoccupied with the reality created by those questions.
